title: [C20T1] - Population changes in New York City and other districts
prompt: The first table below shows changes in the total population of New York City from 1800 to 2000. The second and third tables show changes in the population of the five districts of the city (Manhattan, Brooklyn, Bronx, Queens, Staten Island) over the same period.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The tables illustrate population changes in New York City and its districts from 1800 to 2000, showing both absolute numbers and proportional distributions.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, New York City experienced remarkable population growth over the 200-year period. Meanwhile, Manhattan's dominance significantly declined from being the overwhelming majority to a small minority, while the other districts collectively expanded to become the vast majority.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding New York City as a whole, the population started at a modest 79,216 in 1800. The city experienced steady and dramatic growth throughout the period, with the population surging to 3,437,202 by 1900, representing more than a 40-fold increase in just one century. This upward trend continued into the following century, with the total population reaching 8,009,185 by 2000, marking an overall 100-fold expansion over the 200-year timeframe.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Turning to the district breakdown, Manhattan dominated the city in 1800, accounting for 76% of the total population compared to just 24% for the other four districts combined. However, these proportions reversed dramatically over time. By 2000, Manhattan's share had declined substantially to only 19% of the total population, while the other districts had expanded their collective share to 81%, at 1,538,096 compared to 6,471,089, respectively.
